data.narrative:
ParityQC is a Series A quantum computing company founded by Wolfgang Lechner and Magdalena Hauser. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of 11 firms in quantum computing: 3 public entities (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private companies, including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

Standard peer-median triangulation is not applicable here. The quantum computing sector contains only 5 same-sector peers total, and filtering by stage (Series A), adjacent stage, or valuation tier yields fewer than three datapoints in any single cohort—the minimum threshold required for meaningful median anchoring. A sector-wide median would obscure material differences in technology maturity, deployment stage, and capital intensity across the broader comp set.

Given these constraints, a reliable valuation range cannot be derived from the data provided. Any single-method conclusion would rest on an insufficiently narrow peer cohort. Recommended next steps include: (1) expanding the analysis to earlier-stage quantum companies to establish developmental benchmarks, (2) modeling from first principles using burn rate and runway relative to capital requirements in the sector, or (3) deploying venture capital method frameworks specific to deep-tech hardware development timelines. The absence of sufficient same-stage comparables in a nascent sector remains the binding constraint.
